characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1

characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness ~200 HBW, nearly flat from 0Al to 6Al (Fig. 3d).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; fully recrystallized microstructure with grain size ~20 μm and some retained Mn microsegregations after hot rolling and water quenching.

interfaces.interface_notes: Single-phase austenitic (SIMPLEX) steel; no phase interfaces are reported for this sample.
interfaces.slip_behavior: For 25–30 wt.% Mn and up to 4–5 wt.% Al the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism (dislocation-based strain hardening followed at higher loads by mechanical twinning); after aging at 500–600 °C twinning is reduced and strain hardening is associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: sensitivity of mechanical data to applied aging treatments

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace and were successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks were hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching.
Aging conducted in air at 500 °C for 1 h, followed by oil quenching.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

unmapped_findings: This sample (Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al, aged 500 °C for 1 h) is one condition within the 45-condition RAP matrix for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl system (5 Al contents × 9 heat treatments); results are plotted in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4.

The 4 wt.% Al and 6 wt.% Al alloys are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).

In Fig. 4, the 4Al (blue) points form the lowest-strength clusters at roughly 460–600 MPa tensile strength with elongation spanning ~8% to ~55% across the 4Al aging conditions; the 500 °C, 1 h condition is included but not individually labelled.

κ-carbide (j-carbide) nanoprecipitation upon aging is discussed generally for the Fe-Mn-Al-C system (L'1₂ structure, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC); for this specific 4 wt.% Al sample aged 500 °C for 1 h, the paper does not report direct microstructural evidence of κ-carbides (the detailed APT/TEM analysis in Fig. 5 is for Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al after 24 h at 600 °C).
